Quick technical breakdown (high level) — putting estimated owners and rough ETA here so we have a baseline for the meeting:

- SDK integration (Java + Node): owner = Karthik Iyer (lead engineer), co-owner = Integracom eng (Ashley). Tasks: dependency mapping, sample app, CI smoke tests. ETA: initial PRs by 2027-05-11.
- Server API surface (batch endpoints + streaming proxy): owner = Karthik Iyer. Tasks: agree on auth header semantics, session lifetime, reconnect behavior. ETA: design by 2027-05-07, implementation spike week of 2027-05-10.
- Auth model for streaming: owner = Ben Carter (security/infra), tasks: short-lived session tokens, STS-style exchange, refresh behavior. ETA: spike results by 2027-05-06.
- Tool calling contract tests (webhook + signed payloads): owner = Marissa Cole (CS/partner eng), tasks: integration test harness, replayable test vectors. ETA: harness mid-May, contract tests by 2027-05-20.

Blockers I see now: access to Integracom staging API keys, and a list of the webhook endpoints expected for tool-calling. Lisa — can you confirm those two items before Tuesday?

-Karthik

Irene / team — quick follow-up after reviewing the proposed spikes. Two notes from infra/security perspective:

1) Streaming auth spike scope
- We can validate short-lived token exchange and replay protection in ~2 engineer-days if Integracom can provide a staging token issuer endpoint or a test client secret. Without that, the spike expands to ~4 days due to setup.

2) Tool calling (signed payloads)
- We should standardize on HMAC-SHA256 signatures with a timestamp window; I'll draft a sample verification snippet. Marissa — if you can own the replayable vectors, I can wire verification into our integration tests.

I attached brief notes from my quick exploration. If Integracom can share staging access by EOD Wednesday, we'll proceed with the 2-day spike starting Thursday.

-Ben
Staff Engineer, Platform Security, Redwood Inference
